title: These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef, the yesod that gives
overview:
Chapter 36, *lamed-vav*, opens with *eleh*, which is 36: "These are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef." Yosef is *yesod*, the small *vav*, the *tzaddik* who holds heaven and earth. Understanding something for oneself is not yet *yesod*; *yesod* is the power to bring it to another, and that is why the *tzaddik* is called good: a good guy who never did anyone a favor is no good guy.

To give, one must reach higher than one who only understands: *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is rooted in *Arich* and *Atik*, which is why a teacher learns most from his students. A real *mashpia* does not hand over information; he turns around a person's will, and the Rebbe his whole being, up to the seventy years of *Adam Kadmon* and the *Ein Sof*. A five-minute *mashpia* is no *mashpia*.

Yosef is an orphan from his mother, not his father: *bina* reaches only *hod*, admitting what one should do, as everyone who pays to lose weight or stop smoking already knows. Sight, from *Abba*, reaches *yesod* and moves a person to act. Its height is seeing G-d with the eyes of flesh, as the Alter Rebbe davened with the *shtender*.

sections.title: Yosef, the small vav: the yesod that holds heaven and earth
sections.summary: *Eleh toldos Yaakov Yosef*: Yosef is *yesod*, the higher *tzaddik*, the small *vav*. *Yesod* is what holds heaven and earth together, the *middos* above and *Malchus* below.

phrases.he: (לו) והנה כתיב אלה תולדות יעקב יוסף
שהוא בחינת יסוד, בחינת צדיק עליון כו'
והוא הנקרא וי''ו זעירא כו':

blocks.text: Some of these chapters, and maybe others we don't know about, carry their number in their words. *Lamed-beis* (32) spells *lev*, heart; now, on *lamed-vav* (36), the chapter opens *eleh toldos Yaakov Yosef*, "these are the generations of Yaakov: Yosef." This is the *vav ze'ira* (the small *vav*). *Eleh* is six times six: Yosef is the sixth *sefira*, which has six of its own. He thinks he saw this in the *Zohar*, of the six *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*.

The book is very amazing: it has these little things in it. It was written by the Mitteler Rebbe; "I mean, it was written by G-d, let's put it that way." Things like this can't just happen: *lev* is *lamed-beis*, and *eleh* is *lamed-vav*.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע בענין כי כל בשמים ובארץ
ותרגומו דאחיד בשמיא כו'
phrases.en: He is the connection between the heaven and the earth, meaning between the *middos* and *Malchus*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אור השפע דיסוד צדיק עליון הנקרא חי העולמים כו'

blocks.text: The explanation is known from the verse *Lecha Hashem hagedula*: after *gedula*, *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach* and *hod* comes *ki chol bashamayim uva'aretz*, "for all in heaven and on earth", which is *yesod*, and then "Yours is the kingdom", *Malchus*. The Targum renders it *d'achid bishmaya uv'ar'a*, that holds in heaven and on earth: **he is the connection between the heaven and the earth**. This is the light of the *shefa* (flow) of *yesod*, the higher *tzaddik*, called *Chai ha'olamim*, the life of the worlds.

sections.title: Yesod is the power to give: the tzaddik is good to others
sections.summary: Understanding something for oneself is not yet *yesod*; *yesod* is the power to bring it out to another. That is the *tzaddik*, half in heaven and half on earth, and that is why he is called good: the nature of the good is to do good to someone else.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל, מי שמבין אור השכל לעצמו, אבל אין לו כח להביא אור השכל לידי השפעה לחוץ למקבל
הרי זה עדיין רק בבחינת עצם השפע הזאת כמו שהוא בעצמו

blocks.text: By way of a *mashal*: one who understands the light of the intellect for himself, but has no power to bring it out as an influence to a receiver, still has only the *shefa* itself, as it is in him. This is very close to *tevuna*, which is why *tevuna* has the same shape as a *vav*: it is a long *nun*. *Tevuna* brings the idea down from the inner *sechel* to the outside; *yesod* brings it from himself out to the other person. Basically the same *inyan*, so the same shape, except that one is longer.

phrases.he: אבל מי שיוכל להביאו להשפעה בגלוי למקבלים,
הוא הנקרא בחינת יסוד כו'
phrases.en: That's the *tzaddik*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא כל דאחיד כו'
phrases.en: The *tzaddik*: one side of him is in heaven and the other side is in earth.

phrases.he: שנמשך מן המשפיע אל המקבל

blocks.text: But one who can bring it out openly to the receivers is called *yesod*: **that's the *tzaddik***. The whole thing of a *tzaddik* (a righteous man) is that not only does he have it, he can bring it to others. And he is called *kula d'achid*, the one who holds it all: **one side of him is in heaven and the other side is in earth**.

blocks.title: Moshe, half man and half G-d
blocks.text: As they say, and he thinks it is in the *Zohar* too: Moshe Rabbeinu is called *ish ha'Elokim*, the man of G-d. He was half man, half G-d. That is the *tzaddik*: half of him is up with G-d and the other half is down here, and he holds on in both places, in heaven and on earth.
By the way, he thinks it was the Tzemach Tzedek who said of the Mitteler Rebbe that he was on the level of *ish ha'Elokim*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אור זרוע לצדיק כו'
וכתיב באור כי טוב,
phrases.en: The light, it says, the *Aibershter* saw *ki tov*.

phrases.he: שבחינת יסוד נקרא טוב,
phrases.en: He saw that the light was *yesod*, *tov*.

phrases.he: כמו שמטבע הטוב להטיב לזולתו דוקא
phrases.en: You can't be good just inside of yourself: *teva hatov* is *lehativ* to somebody else.

phrases.he: כך בחינת יסוד נקרא צדיק וטוב,
כמו שכתוב אמרו צדיק כי טוב,
phrases.en: Say to the *tzaddik* that he's good.

phrases.he: וצדיק צדקות אהב כו',
phrases.en: That he liked *tzedaka*, to help people.

phrases.he: להחיות רוח שפלים כו'
phrases.en: To be *mechayeh* the spirit of the lowly people, people who don't have.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב טוב יהו״ה לכל כו'
phrases.en: The *Aibershter* is *mashpia* to everybody.

blocks.text: As it says, *or zarua latzaddik*, "light is sown for the *tzaddik*". And of the light it says **the *Aibershter* saw *ki tov***, that it was good: **He saw that the light was *yesod*, *tov***. *Yesod* is called good, for the nature of the good is to do good, and the word is *davka* (specifically): to someone else.

blocks.title: The good guy who kicks the dogs
blocks.text: What does it mean, he's a good guy? **You can't be good just inside of yourself: *teva hatov* is *lehativ* to somebody else**. If he never did anybody a favor in his life, what kind of a good guy is he, even if inside he's good? Even Americans say that someone who runs around shouting at the kids and kicking all the dogs can't be so good. He's a *chassidishe* guy, he really meditates? So what? He shouts at all the kids.

So *yesod* is called *tzaddik* and good, because he gives to the other. As it says, *imru tzaddik ki tov*: **say to the *tzaddik* that he's good**. And *tzaddik tzedakos ahev*: what is a *tzaddik*? **That he liked *tzedaka*, to help people**; **to be *mechayeh* the spirit of the lowly people**, those who don't have. And *tov Hashem lakol*: **the *Aibershter* is *mashpia* to everybody**.

sections.title: Seventeen, peace and covenant: Yosef the inner yesod, Noach the outer
sections.summary: *V'tov* is seventeen, the number of Yosef, and the initials of "the heaven and the earth": the bond of giver and receiver. *Yesod* is also peace and covenant; Yosef is its inside and Noach its outside, and the difference is a whole mitzva.

phrases.he: (וטוב גימטריא י''ז שהוא א''ה ו''ה, ר''ת דאת השמים ואת הארץ,
דהיינו דאחיד בשמיא וארעא כו'
phrases.en: That means he's holding the heaven and the earth.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת התקשרות המשפיע במקבל כידוע ומבואר במקום אחר

blocks.text: *V'tov* (and good) is seventeen in *gematria*, the number of Yosef. It is *alef-hei vav-hei*: add it up, six and eleven, and you get seventeen. These are the initials of *es hashamayim v'es ha'aretz*, "the heaven and the earth": **that means he's holding the heaven and the earth**.

This is the bond of the *mashpia* (giver) with the *mekabel* (receiver), as explained elsewhere. And by Yosef it says he was seventeen years old; then, he thinks, he was away from his father seventeen years, and his father was with him another seventeen, for Yaakov lived another seventeen years after he came down. It is all seventeen, the number of Yosef.

phrases.he: ונקרא גם כן שלום וברית,
phrases.en: It's also called peace and the *bris*.

phrases.he: כמו בפנחס, הנני נותן לו את בריתי שלום
כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בהפרש שבין פנימיות יסוד זעיר אנפין כיוסף, לחיצוניות יסוד שהוא בחינת נח, צדיק תמים, כמו שכתוב בזהר)
והיינו ו' זעירא שהוא בחינת הקיבוץ ואסיפת אור ושפע של המדות דיעקב הנזכר לעיל.

blocks.text: *Yesod* is also called *shalom* and *bris*: **it's also called peace and the *bris*** (covenant), as with Pinchas, "Behold, I give him My covenant of peace." And, as explained elsewhere, there is the difference between the inner *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, Yosef, and the outer *yesod*, Noach, *tzaddik tamim* (a perfect *tzaddik*), as the *Zohar* says. It is like Yisroel and Yaakov: Yosef is in *yesod* what Yisroel is in *tiferes*, and Noach is like Yaakov.

blocks.question: Yaakov and Yisroel are the same man; Yosef and Noach are two. Is that not a much bigger difference?
blocks.text: There is. One may say it is not a matter of Jew and non-Jew: Yosef too was a *ben Noach* (a son of Noach), and Noach also had the Jewish soul. But Yosef was circumcised. And if Noach was born circumcised? No difference: he had no mitzva. Yosef too was born circumcised, by the way, but he had the mitzva, so he needed *hatafas dam* (the drawing of a drop of blood). Having a mitzva is a whole different thing.

phrases.he: וזהו אלה תולדות יעקב יוסף,
בחינת התולדה של המדות על ידי יוסף דוקא,
phrases.en: The whole *tolda* of the *middos* into action has to go through *yesod*.

phrases.he: שהוא אור הזרוע לצדיק ח''י עלמין כו'

blocks.text: So *eleh toldos Yaakov Yosef*: the *tolda* (offspring) of the *middos* comes through Yosef *davka*, the light sown for the *tzaddik*, the life of the worlds. **The whole *tolda* of the *middos* into action has to go through *yesod***.

sections.title: Rooted above the intellect: the palm tree, the teacher, and what a mashpia gives
sections.summary: *Yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* is rooted in the *yesod* of *Arich* and *Atik*, above the intellect, so one who gives to others must reach higher than one who only understands. A real *mashpia* does not teach information: he turns around a person's will, and a great one his whole being.

phrases.he: וכתיב צדיק כתמר כו' כארז בלבנון,
ששרש יסוד זעיר אנפין הוא ביסוד דאריך אנפין ועתיק יומין שלמעלה מן השכל כו'
phrases.en: The *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, in order to really be *mashpia* to other people, has to have its root in *yesod* of *Arich* and *Atik*, which is totally higher than the *sechel*.

blocks.text: *Tzaddik katamar yifrach, k'erez baLevanon yisgeh*: "the *tzaddik* will flourish like a palm, grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon." The root of the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, the palm, is in the *yesod* of *Arich Anpin* and *Atik Yomin*, above the intellect. That is why the *tzaddik* can bring it down, as it explains that only a *chacham mufla* (a wondrous sage), who has the *chachma* all the way to its source, can bring it down. **The *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, in order to really be *mashpia* to other people, has to have its root in *yesod* of *Arich* and *Atik***: understanding the *sechel* itself is not enough.

It is *nautz techilasan b'sofan* (their beginning is wedged in their end). It is also why it says *mikol melamdai hiskalti*: "I learned more from my students than from my teachers." When he understands for himself, he only has to understand the idea as it is. *Davka* when he teaches others, it is a matter of *yesod*, and so he has to reach higher than the *sechel* itself: the lower he goes, the higher he has to reach.

In terms of *bina* and *tevuna*, *davka* this activates the *tevuna*. Basically *hisbonenus* (contemplation) activates it too, and the fourth part discusses at length contemplation from above to below and from below to above. But contemplating for himself basically activates the *bina*, and even the *tevuna* may stay with it: the *meshalim* he brings up are still only for himself, because "nobody ever asked him a stupid question." *Davka* when he has to explain it to somebody else does the long *nun* of *tevuna* really come down.

phrases.he: כי נעוץ תחלתן בסופן כי יסוד נקרא סיומא דגופא כו'
ועל כן עיקר התענוג בכלות השפע דוקא,
phrases.en: The main *taanug* that people like is when the *shefa* comes out from the *yesod*.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין ויכל אלהי״ם כו'

blocks.text: For their beginning is wedged in their end: *yesod* is called *siyuma d'gufa*, the end of the body. So the main delight is *davka* at the conclusion of the *shefa*: **the main *taanug* that people like is when the *shefa* comes out from the *yesod***, which touches the essence of the delight. In physical terms, the biggest physical pleasure, the one everybody runs after, is when the *shefa* comes out of the *yesod*. And so with *vayechal Elokim*, "and G-d finished": at the end of the *shefa* He said *ki tov me'od*, "very good"; then He had a big enjoyment.

phrases.he: (והיינו שהיה יוסף יפה תואר כו'
phrases.en: *Yosef* was very handsome.

phrases.he: מעין שופריה דיעקב,
phrases.en: He was like the beauty of *Yaakov*,

phrases.he: בחינת תפארת דזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: meaning *tiferes* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: ושופריה דיעקב מעין שופריה דאדם קדמאה,
phrases.en: *Yaakov*'s beauty was like the beauty of *Adam HaRishon*,

phrases.he: בחינת אריך אנפין ואדם קדמון כו')
phrases.en: meaning *Arich* and even *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: **Yosef was very handsome**: **he was like the beauty of *Yaakov***, **meaning *tiferes* of *Zeir Anpin***, for *yesod* is the same as *tiferes*. And **Yaakov's beauty was like the beauty of *Adam HaRishon***, **meaning *Arich* and even *Adam Kadmon***.

So a *mashpia* must give at least from *Arich*. What is a *mashpia*? Not one who teaches mathematics, or even the intellect of *Chassidus*: that is not a real *mashpia*. A *mashpia* gives the *ratzon* (will). You give him this *putz*, and he turns him into a guy with a *ratzon* for *Chassidus* and *darkei haChassidus* (the Chassidic ways).

sensitivity.reason: A Yiddish vulgarity for the person the mashpia turns around.
sensitivity.publishable: So a *mashpia* must give at least from *Arich*. What is a *mashpia*? Not one who teaches mathematics, or even the intellect of *Chassidus*: that is not a real *mashpia*. A *mashpia* gives the *ratzon* (will). You give him this guy, and he turns him into a guy with a *ratzon* for *Chassidus* and *darkei haChassidus* (the Chassidic ways).

blocks.text: Even a rabbi has some kind of influence on his congregation, that they should walk in the right path, whatever their path is. But the main influence is not learning intellectual things with them; it is an influence from *Arich*.

But there's a *tzaddik* and there's a *tzaddik*. A big *mashpia* can give from *Adam Kadmon*: he can take a person and turn his whole *Adam Kadmon* around. This is by the *shluchim* (emissaries) of the Rebbe. And by the Rebbe himself it can go even higher: the *yesod* can go all the way to the *yesod* of the *Ein Sof*.

sections.title: From the delight of the Essence to the hyssop in the wall
sections.summary: No offspring without new *mochin* reaching the inner delight. The *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* comes from the *yesod* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop in the wall; and the *tzaddik* who flourishes like a palm rises to the seventy years of *Adam Kadmon*, where it is infinite.

phrases.he: ומה שכתוב אלה תולדות, היינו בחינת ו׳ קצוות דזעיר אנפין שכלול כל אחד מו', שעולה גימטריא אלה אך אין תולדה בלא תוספת מוחין חדשים מאבא ואמא על ידי בחינת הגדלות דכחב''ד שבזעיר אנפין כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: And *eleh toldos*: here the text says it itself. It is the six directions of *Zeir Anpin*, each including six, and *eleh* is that number in *gematria*: 36, the number of this chapter, *lamed-vav*.

But there is no *tolda* without an addition of new *mochin* (intellect) from *Abba* and *Ima*, through the *gadlus* (maturity) of *Kachab* in *Zeir Anpin*. *Davka* through it, it goes all the way into the *pnimiyus hataanug* (the inner delight). So with a physical offspring: if it does not go into the inner delight, there won't be any *tolda*.

He won't have any children. As he explains in *Tanya*, the drop comes out of the brain, and that is why it has the encoding in it and he can beget. Begetting is not like explaining to somebody else: it *mamash* brings over the essence, not just the ideas in the brain but the physicality of the brain itself.

phrases.he: (ובזה יש גם כן בחינת ההתבוננות אחת כוללת מן הרבה פרטים בכלל אחד,
שהוא מיסוד דמלכות דאין סוף עד בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין
phrases.en: It really goes from the *yesod* of *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*; this comes down to *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: (על דרך הנזכר לעיל בזעיר אנפין בכלל,
phrases.en: The same like we said in chapter 33 in *Zeir Anpin* in general.

phrases.he: שהוא סוף עולם האין סוף כו')

blocks.text: Here there is also one contemplation that gathers many particulars into one whole: from the *yesod* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* to the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*. As said before, by the Rebbe it really goes all the way, and even higher, for *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* goes all the way to *Yachid*. **It really goes from the *yesod* of *Malchus* of *Ein Sof***: the influence of the *Aibershter*, Who wanted to be *mashpia* to the world. And this comes down to the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*.

**The same like we said in chapter 33 in *Zeir Anpin* in general**: it is the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. That is in general; in particular, the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* comes from the *yesod* of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב וידבר שלמה מן הארז אשר בלבנון, בעצם התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט אנא אמלוך כו'
עד בחינת האזוב אשר בקיר,
שהוא בחינת וי''ו זעירא דקטנות יסוד זעיר אנפין בהשפעתו והתקשרותו במלכות שנקרא קיר
phrases.en: The *ezov* is *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, and the *kir* is the *Malchus*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב ויתפלל כו' אל הקיר,
phrases.en: He davened to the wall.

phrases.he: וכן נעשה נא עליית קיר, שהוא בחינת המלכות כמו שכתוב בזהר

blocks.text: As it says, *Vayedaber Shlomo min ha'erez asher baLevanon*, "Shlomo spoke from the cedar in Lebanon": in the essence of the simple delight in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, when it arose in His simple will, *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule). *Levanon* is from *loven*, whiteness, like the *or tzach umetzuchtzach*, the pure and polished light.

*Ad ha'ezov asher bakir*, down to the hyssop in the wall: this means Shlomo also read this book, and so he could tell you everything from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop in the wall. It is the small *vav*: **the *ezov* is *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, and the *kir* is the *Malchus***, the small *vav* of the *katnus* (immaturity) of the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, in its influence and its bond with *Malchus*, which is called a wall.

blocks.question: *Vayispallel el hakir*: he davened to the wall? What kind of *avoda zara* is that?
blocks.text: The wall is *Malchus*, as in *na'aseh na aliyas kir*, "let us make a walled upper room", as the *Zohar* explains.

phrases.he: והיינו צדיק כתמר דסליק לע' שנין דאדם קדמון,
phrases.en: He has to go up to the 70 years of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: ששם כארז בלבנון ישגה בבחינת אין סוף ממש ודי למבין)
phrases.en: There, it's totally infinite.

blocks.text: That is *tzaddik katamar yifrach*, rising to the seventy years of *Adam Kadmon*. What does it mean that the *tzaddik*, the *mashpia*, has to flourish, to grow bigger? **He has to go up to the 70 years of *Adam Kadmon***.

blocks.title: The five-minute mashpia
blocks.text: Otherwise, what kind of *mashpia* is he? Even the *rav* of any congregation is trying to influence the people for their whole seventy years; otherwise he is not a *mashpia*. Did it work? "Yeah, I was *mashpia* on him for five minutes." And afterwards? "Well, I'm a five-minute *mashpia*." If you're a five-minute *mashpia*, you're not a *mashpia* at all.

A real *mashpia* goes up, *d'salik*, to the seventy years of *Adam Kadmon*. When he is there, *k'erez baLevanon yisgeh*, in the aspect of the *Ein Sof* itself: **there, it's totally infinite**. When he goes up to *Adam Kadmon*, the influence becomes totally infinite.

That is the matter of a Rebbe. Rabbis of congregations don't *mamash* go up there: they get from *Adam Kadmon* as it comes through *Arich* and through the intellect. Still, the root has to be in *Adam Kadmon*, or he is no *mashpia*. But a real *tzaddik*, like the Rebbe, goes *mamash* up there, *k'erez baLevanon yisgeh*, and past it, all the way to the *Ein Sof*.

sections.title: An orphan from his mother: understanding stops at hod, seeing reaches yesod
sections.summary: Yosef is an orphan from his mother, not his father: understanding (*bina*) reaches only *hod*, admitting what one should do, while sight, from *Abba*, reaches *yesod* and moves a person to act, even after the contemplation has gone. The highest sight sees G-d with physical eyes, as the Alter Rebbe saw the *shtender*.

phrases.he: (וגם עוד מבואר במקום אחר שיוסף נקרא יתום מאמו ולא מאביו כו'
phrases.en: He was a *yasom* from his mother, but not from his father.

phrases.he: ר''ת יתום יפה תאר כו'

blocks.text: It is also explained elsewhere that Yosef is called *yasom* (an orphan) from his mother and not from his father. *Yasom* is the initials of *yefe to'ar vifeh mar'eh*, "handsome of form and handsome to look at." And what does it mean? **He was a *yasom* from his mother, but not from his father**.

phrases.he: וענין יתום מאמו היינו לפי שבחינת יסוד אימא קצר ומסתלק ונעלם בתולדות המדות, כנראה בחוש שבהתפעלות המדות מסתלק השכל כו'
ולזה אמר דבינה רק עד הוד דזעיר אנפין אתפשטת, ולא עד יסוד זעיר אנפין שזהו רק עד בחינת ההודאה שבאה מצד השכל
ולא בבחינת יסוד דזעיר אנפין, שהוא בחינת ההתקשרות עצמיות שבלב, שבו מאיר מבחינת יסוד אבא

blocks.text: What does it mean, an orphan from his mother? The *yesod* of *Ima* is short: it departs and is hidden in the offspring of the *middos*, as one sees that when the *middos* are stirred, the intellect departs. So it says that *bina* spreads only to the *hod* of *Zeir Anpin*, not to its *yesod*: the power of the explanation reaches only to *hoda'a* (acknowledgement), which comes from the intellect, and not to the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, the essential bond in the heart, where the *yesod* of *Abba* shines.

phrases.he: בחינת התקשרות בעצם אור המושכל קודם שבא להשגה,
והיינו לבי ראה הרבה חכמה כו',
ראיית השכל שבלב בשר ביסוד זעיר אנפין דוקא

blocks.title: Richard Simmons
blocks.text: It is a bond with the very light of the concept, before it comes to comprehension. How *bina* goes only to *hod* you can see from Richard Simmons, who makes a lot of money. Why? Because *bina* only goes to *hod*. Who goes to him? A bunch of fat ladies who want to get skinny. They understand it's good for their health, they'll look pretty, they'll buy clothes for a third of the price; that's why they go. If they understand it so well, why don't they do it? Because *bina* only goes to *hod*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the women who go to a weight-loss program "fat ladies".
sensitivity.publishable: It is a bond with the very light of the concept, before it comes to comprehension. How *bina* goes only to *hod* you can see from Richard Simmons, who makes a lot of money. Why? Because *bina* only goes to *hod*. Who goes to him? People who want to lose weight. They understand it's good for their health, they'll look better, they'll buy clothes for a third of the price; that's why they go. If they understand it so well, why don't they do it? Because *bina* only goes to *hod*.

blocks.title: Smoking, dieting and the self-help books
blocks.text: Or a guy who goes to one of these places to stop smoking, because he understands it's bad for him, or a guy who goes to a muscle-builder. You see it all over the place, in all the self-help books: if they understand it's good to diet, to build up muscles, to stop smoking, why don't they do it? They understand fine.

They even understand to the point that they are *modeh* (admit it): "I know, I know I got to stop smoking," or the fat lady: "I really got to lose some weight; I shouldn't be eating this piece of cheesecake." So why are you eating it? Because the intellectual understanding goes only to *hod*: they admit it from the intellect's decision, but that is not enough to bring it out. *Yesod* goes into *Malchus*; this does not reach *yesod*, so it does not come out to the outside.

sensitivity.reason: Calls a woman trying to lose weight "the fat lady".
sensitivity.publishable: They even understand to the point that they are *modeh* (admit it): "I know, I know I got to stop smoking," or the woman on a diet: "I really got to lose some weight; I shouldn't be eating this piece of cheesecake." So why are you eating it? Because the intellectual understanding goes only to *hod*: they admit it from the intellect's decision, but that is not enough to bring it out. *Yesod* goes into *Malchus*; this does not reach *yesod*, so it does not come out to the outside.

blocks.title: The smoker's lung
blocks.text: It has to be in a way of seeing: when it is seen, that does affect the *yesod*. At the seminars that help smokers go from *hoda'a* to action, one thing they do is show them pictures of a smoker's lung and a healthy lung. Many times, when people see this with their eyes, which is already a matter of *chachma*, they say "Wow!", and it changes them over.

blocks.title: Richard Simmons and the old pants
blocks.text: In any Richard Simmons show, half the show everybody jumps up and down to music. The other half is always the skinny lady and a picture of how she used to be. Everybody says "Oh!", she cries, Richard Simmons hugs her and cries: she used to be 230 pounds. They bring her old pants and she stands inside them, and other fat ladies look and say, "Look at her pants, look at my pants: I could also be like that." It is a matter of *re'iya* (sight).

blocks.text: Sight affects. And it is not only to sell you on it: even in the actual classes, where people already paid, you'd think the class would be just jumping up and down, but half of it is ladies brought up on stage who already lost weight, with special visual techniques, like standing with both legs in one leg of the old pants. They see that it works. It is not just an intellectual *havana* (understanding): they had that before the seminar, and that is why they paid the money. They knew intellectually that they should lose weight, but couldn't bring it into action, because intellectual understanding, the *hasaga*, goes only to *hod*.

blocks.text: The actual bond with the thing comes *davka* from *Abba*: when you see it. *Libi ra'ah harbeh chachma*, "my heart has seen much wisdom": the sight of the intellect in the heart of flesh, in *yesod*. As there they have to see it, so here he speaks of sight. This all goes back to the chapters on *tevuna*, chapters 2 and 3: the *re'iyas hasechel* (sight of the intellect), *l'istakla bikra d'malka* (to gaze at the glory of the King), and "in the eye of the intellect in the heart, everything is seen."

The *tevuna* comes *davka* from a matter of *chachma* in which he sees the thing; it is not the same as just understanding. There is understanding, and understanding within the understanding, when he gets to the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept): it must be so. That brings to *hoda'a*: you admit you really should be a Chassidic guy and so on, but nothing will happen from it, without the *tevuna*.

Then the *daas*, the actual bond of the intellect with the thing, goes into the *chachma* and brings an actual seeing: not only that it must be so, but that this is how it is. That is with the eye of the intellect, not with eyes of flesh. Higher still, the *tevuna* goes deeper into the *chachma*: *re'iya b'einei basar*, sight with eyes of flesh, literally looking at G-d with physical eyes.

blocks.title: The ninja
blocks.text: How is that possible? He has no body and no likeness of a body. It is like a ninja who comes into the room: dressed all in black so he can sneak around in the dark, head and hands covered, a mask over the whole face, with little holes for the eyes. You say a guy came in here. Someone says you saw nothing, just clothing; you think he's crazy: you saw a guy come in, a ninja. So when he sees the world, he literally sees G-d.

blocks.title: Davening with the shtender
blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe asked the Mitteler Rebbe what he had davened with, and he said: with something of *Adam Kadmon*. The Mitteler Rebbe asked, "And you?" The Alter Rebbe said, "I davened with the *shtender* (lectern)." What does that mean? They explain that he *mamash* saw how the *shtender* is *mamash* G-dliness, just an outer garment. He *mamash* saw it.

This is no longer the mind's eye but the physical eye. With the ninja too you see only the clothing, yet it is beyond understanding logically, or even seeing with the mind's eye, that someone must be inside: you actually see a person there, totally enclothed. So the Alter Rebbe, seeing the physical world, sees the actual G-dliness *mamash* with physical eyes. That is *libi ra'ah harbeh chachma*: the sight of the intellect in the heart of flesh, in the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* *davka*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הביטול שנמשך בהבל חזה הלב,
כמו שכתוב ברעייא מהימנא בעין השכל, דבלבא אתחזי כולא כו'
phrases.en: In the eye of the *sechel* in the heart, he sees everything.

blocks.text: It is the *bittul* (self-nullification) drawn into the breath of the chest of the heart, in the lungs: the actual sight of the thing comes all the way into the inner *middos*. As in the *Ra'aya Mehemna*: **in the eye of the *sechel* in the heart, he sees everything**. The heart, by the way, is *bina*; but in *bina* there is a deeper level, which goes up from the contemplation into the inner *chachma*.

phrases.he: לפי שיסוד אבא ארוך משל אימא, ונמשך עד בחינת יסוד זעיר אנפין
גם לאחר שנסתלק אור הבינה
phrases.en: Even after the *or habina* is gone.

phrases.he: על כן נקרא יתום מאמו ולא מאביו וכו'
phrases.en: That's why he was a *yasom* only from his mother, but not from his father.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב ביאור זה במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: Because the *yesod* of *Abba* is longer than that of *Ima*: when you see something, it goes down to *yesod*. It reaches the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, the actual effect on the emotion, the urge to do something, to bring the thing out into action. And **even after the *or habina* is gone**: he can still see it once he is no longer contemplating it.
So Yosef is called **a *yasom* only from his mother, but not from his father**: he did have his father. This is explained elsewhere at length.

phrases.he: והיינו גם כן ענין אלה תולדות יעקב, בחינת טיפת יסוד אבא, הוא יוסף יסוד זעיר אנפין כו' ודי למבין):

blocks.text: This is also *eleh toldos Yaakov*: the drop of the *yesod* of *Abba*. In Yaakov, *Yisroel Saba*, there is the inside, called Yisroel, and the outside, *Nehi*, called Yaakov. Yosef, the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, comes from the *yesod* of *Abba*, and the *yesod* of *Abba* comes down into it. And that's chapter 36.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is understanding something for oneself not yet *yesod*, and why is the *tzaddik* called good?
Why does one who teaches others have to reach higher than one who understands for himself?
What does a real *mashpia* give, and how does a Rebbe differ from the *rav* of a congregation?
What does it mean that *bina* reaches only to *hod*, and what do the people who pay to lose weight or stop smoking show about it?
What is seeing G-d with eyes of flesh, and how do the ninja and the Alter Rebbe's *shtender* explain it?
Why is Yosef an orphan from his mother and not from his father?

notes.text: He says, with "I think", that Yosef was away from his father seventeen years; by the verses he was seventeen when sold and Yaakov came down when Yosef was thirty-nine, so twenty-two years. The block keeps his words and his hesitation.

He renders *mikol melamdai hiskalti* (Tehillim 119:99, "from all my teachers I gained understanding") as "I learned more from my students than from my teachers", the reading of the Gemara (Taanis 7a). Kept as he said it.

Class 204 jumps in its times from 15:01 (w1999-2003) to 15:17 (w2004-2022) and then to 18:05 (w2023): about three minutes of the tape have almost no transcribed words. The block on w2004-2066 is written from what is there; a reviewer should listen to 15:00-18:10 for anything the transcript missed.

Not flagged, as physiology that only explains the line (STYLE.md): the main physical pleasure is when the *shefa* comes out of the *yesod* (204 w1764-1821), and the drop that comes from the brain, from *Tanya* (204 w2237-2343). A reviewer may want to look at them for a public edition.

The Yosef-and-Noach discussion (204 w1062-1273) comes after the alignment mark for line 16, but it explains line 15 (the inner and outer *yesod*), so lines 14-16 are one passage. He rereads line 16 at w1274-1286 (omitted as reading).
In the question on Yosef and Noach, "Noach was born *mahul*" (w1206-1209) may be a listener's objection; the transcript does not say, so the block gives it as an objection with no speaker.
The phrase on line 30 cites his English (w3014-3026), which comes after he reads line 31.
"They'll still be only in his own era" (204 w1627-1648) is read as "area" and written "only for himself".

Richard Simmons is named as an example only (his shows, his money), not criticised, so there is no named-person flag; the three flags are for "fat ladies". Class 205 opens by going on with the mashal before rereading line 36 (w422).

His readings differ from the printed text in small ways: line 23 "כתר חב\"ד" for כחב"ד (the block writes *Kachab*), line 33 "פשטה" for אתפשטת, and line 37 "מה שאין כן ברעיא מהימנא" for "כמו שכתוב ברעייא מהימנא" (possibly the transcript). The lines stay as printed.
